notes: Positions come from a greedy bottom-left-fill over no-fit polygons; the result is a good layout, not a proven optimum.

Nesting polygons circumscribe the true arcs (0.3 mm tolerance), are simplified by 0.05 mm and grown conservatively, so parts are never closer than the spacing but may end up to 0.30 mm farther apart than needed; the independent verifier checks the exact contours afterwards.
Part spacing is a geometric clearance between contours. Kerf is NOT compensated here — the machine's program must apply it, once.
Utilization = Σ outer-contour areas of the placed parts ÷ sheet area (holes count as used material).
